state:
Goal `core-ratelimit-and-3-more`. `Core\RateLimit::consume` has all its feature proofs: `about.md`, three examples, one attack, a Rust test carrying its `covers:` marker, and a perf skip in `data/proofs/policy.json` that follows `Core\Cache::shared`'s, because the sweep runs no store. `Core\RateLimit` and `Core\RateLimit\Decision` both carry class cards now, so neither is in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.
No shared store is reachable from an example, an attack or a bench. Every `consume` call there throws the `cache.shared` capability refusal. `shed` needs no store, which is why `consume`'s third example falls back to it.

items.text: **`Core\RateLimit::shed`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests. It runs in-process, so its bench is real: chain the key off the running total and declare iterations. `shed_is_per_core_and_approximate_and_says_so` and `shed_is_the_same_gcra_over_the_cores_own_memory` exist and only need a `// covers:` marker. `rule:core-classes/ratelimit-two-members`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ratelimit.rs:182`

**`Core\RateLimit\Decision::allowed`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests. The class card is already written. Build decisions through `shed`, since `consume` cannot answer without a store. `rule:core-classes/ratelimit-gcra`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ratelimit.rs:327`

backlog: `consume`'s examples can show only the unconfigured refusal and the `shed` fallback. A loopback store fixture for `docs/examples/` would let them show a real decision — `docs/examples/README.md` § *A grant the examples need*.
